claim: In Russian doll caching, nested records are managed with their own cache keys, and the top-level resource is a collection of those cache keys.
question: What is Russian doll caching?

values.display: nested records are managed with their own cache keys
the top-level resource is a collection of those cache keys

evidence.quote: A newer pattern, Russian doll caching, has come out of work done by the Ruby on Rails team. In this pattern, nested records are managed with their own cache keys, and then the top-level resource is a collection of those cache keys.

claim: With lazy population, objects are automatically added to a new cache node when the application first requests them, and expiring a cached object is as simple as deleting it so the next request fetches a new one from the database.
question: What does lazy caching do when new cache nodes come online, and how is an object expired?

values.display: automatically add objects to the new cache nodes when the application first requests them
Cache expiration is easily handled by simply deleting the cached object

evidence.quote: As new cache nodes come online, for example as your application scales up, the lazy population method will automatically add objects to the new cache nodes when the application first requests them.
Cache expiration is easily handled by simply deleting the cached object. A new object will be fetched from the database the next time it is requested.

claim: In the Valkey and Redis OSS pub/sub paradigm, you send a message to a channel without knowing who receives it; the recipients are those subscribed to the channel.
question: How does Valkey or Redis OSS pub/sub messaging work?

values.display: you send a message to a specific channel not knowing who, if anyone, receives it
those who are subscribed to the channel

evidence.quote: In the Valkey and Redis OSS pub/sub paradigm, you send a message to a specific channel not knowing who, if anyone, receives it. The people who get the message are those who are subscribed to the channel.

claim: Multi-AZ and the append-only file (AOF) are mutually exclusive on ElastiCache for Redis OSS: if you enable one, you cannot enable the other.
question: Can Multi-AZ and AOF be enabled together?

values.display: Multi-AZ and append-only file (AOF) are mutually exclusive
If you enable one, you can't enable the other

qualifiers.scope: ElastiCache for Redis OSS replication groups

evidence.quote: ElastiCache for Redis OSS Multi-AZ and append-only file (AOF) are mutually exclusive. If you enable one, you can't enable the other.

claim: Automatic failover can be enabled without Multi-AZ, but replicas are then not guaranteed to be in different Availability Zones, so it does not protect against AZ-level failures.
question: Does automatic failover without Multi-AZ protect against an Availability Zone failure?

values.display: replicas are not guaranteed to be in different Availability Zones
does not protect against AZ-level failures

qualifiers.scope: Valkey and Redis OSS replication groups

evidence.quote: While it is possible to have automatic failover enabled without Multi-AZ, replicas are not guaranteed to be in different Availability Zones in this configuration. Failover still promotes a replica to primary if one is available, but this does not protect against AZ-level failures.

claim: Multi-AZ is supported on all Valkey and Redis OSS versions, and only on clusters with more than one node in each shard.
question: Which engines and cluster layouts support Multi-AZ?

values.display: Multi-AZ is supported on all Valkey and Redis OSS versions
more than one node in each shard

evidence.quote: Multi-AZ is supported on all Valkey and Redis OSS versions.
Multi-AZ is only supported on Valkey and Redis OSS clusters with more than one node in each shard.
